the eichler encyclopedia interesting facts about hippopotamus 1 they secrete blood sweat hippos dont sweat as we do instead they produce a thick red fluid from their skin its not actually blood it is a specialized liquid that acts as a natural sunscreen moisturizer and antibiotic it starts clear turns orangered within minutes and eventually becomes a crusty brown 2 they cant actually swim despite spending up to 16 hours a day in the water hippos are too dense to swim or even float instead they walk or jog along the river bottom they are so heavy that they just push off the ground essentially leaping through the water in slow motion 3 the deadliest vegetarians while they mostly eat grass hippos are the deadliest large land mammal in africa they are incredibly territorial and unpredictable they cause more human fatalities per year than lions elephants or rhinosusually by capsizing boats or chasing people who get between them and the safety of the water 4 selfsharpening teeth a hippos lower canines can grow to be over 15 feet long these teeth never stop growing and they stay razorsharp because they constantly rub against the smaller upper teeth essentially honing the blade every time the hippo opens and closes its mouth 5 they sleepbreath automatically hippos have a reflex that allows them to rise to the surface take a breath and sink back down without ever waking up they can hold their breath for about five minutes and their ears and nostrils have specialized valves that snap shut the moment they submerge 6 their closest relatives are whales for a long time people thought hippos were related to pigs however dna testing shows that their closest living relatives are actually cetaceans whales and dolphins they split from a common ancestor roughly 55 million years ago 7 species then now the two species alive today right now there are only two living species of hippos left on earth the common hippopotamus this is the large aggressive waterloving giant everyone recognizes the pygmy hippopotamus this is a much smaller reclusive cousin found in the forests of west africa they are about the size of a large pig and spend much more time on land than their bigger relatives the extinct species historically the hippo family was much more diverse while the exact number of prehistoric species is debated by paleontologists there were at least three to four other species that lived alongside early humans before going extinct the madagascar hippos until about 1000 years ago there were as many as three different species of dwarf hippos living on the island of madagascar they likely went extinct due to a combination of climate change and hunting by early human settlers the european hippo during the pleistocene era the ice age a massive species of hippo lived throughout europeeven in what is now england as the climate cooled and ice sheets moved south they eventually died out the giant hippo some prehistoric versions like hippopotamus gorgops were significantly larger than the ones we see today with eyes positioned much higher on their skulls to help them see while almost entirely submerged summary in the distant past there were at least six or seven distinct species spread across africa europe and asia today we are down to just two and both are facing threats from habitat loss and poaching

executive order 14158 establishing the department of government efficiency or doge the basic premise was hard to dispute in fiscal year 2024 the us ran a 18 trillion deficit and debt held by the public stood at 283 trillion if you are already borrowing at that scale stop wasting taxpayers money is hardly a fringe belief doge quickly paired that principle with examples of waste that sounded like parody like a 33k usda contract for guatemala youth conservation corps development consultants or a 144k usda contract for a mexico sustainable landscapes consultant it was not long before the problems started despite the name doge was not a cabinet department created by congress with a senateconfirmed secretary and budgetary authority that survives a news cycle it was created by executive order and could be reshaped or extinguished just as easily by another order next was credibility doges public face was elon musk that made it louder but also made it political personal and brittle even on its own terms doges accounting quickly became disputed doge claimed 55bn of savings early on while a reuters analysis of the partial data it had released suggested contract cuts were really worth c 85bn the third problem was basic governing competence reporting at the time described key doge staff as extremely young and with little to no government experience one widelycited report identified six key individuals in influential roles aged 19 to 24 predictably the project did not settle into durable machinery musk formally stepped down on 28 may 2025 by november 2025 reuters reported that doge doesnt exist having been disbanded well before its scheduled end with former staff moved into other roles and functions absorbed elsewhere so doge leaves a useful lesson yes government wastes money but the real failure was design a serious efficiency programme cannot be a celebrityled executiveorder contraption that hunts for viral contracts and calls it a statecraft revolution if you want longterm gains you need something institutional cabinetlevel and boring in the right way todays essay is an attempt to steelman doge to show what it could have been how deep the rot goes a true attempt to roll back unnecessary parts of the state must not just look at unnecessary spending but unnecessary laws and the process that creates them to take an example in the uk the national building regulations were introduced in 1965 and ran to eight pages today the statutory regulations sit atop a mass of approved documents and guidance running to well over a thousand pages daily reading article for varc practice selfhealing roads a new era in infrastructure as global infrastructure continues to age under the strain of increasing urbanization climate stress and growing traffic loads a revolutionary concept is beginning to take hold selfhealing roads these advanced road materials are designed to autonomously repair cracks and surface damage dramatically extending the lifespan of roads and reducing the need for constant costly maintenance what once sounded like a futuristic idea is now progressing rapidly through research labs and pilot projects across the world the core problem with traditional road surfaces whether made of asphalt or concrete is that they naturally deteriorate over time factors like temperature shifts water infiltration and mechanical stress from vehicles lead to the formation of microcracks left untreated these small imperfections expand into larger structural problems causing potholes surface wear and eventually full road failure conventional repairs are expensive timeconsuming and disruptive selfhealing technology offers a powerful alternative by preventing damage before it becomes visible and critical several advanced approaches are being explored to make this vision a reality one of the most developed techniques involves the incorporation of steel fibers into asphalt mixtures these fibers are conductive and can be heated using electromagnetic induction when cracks form applying induction heat softens the surrounding asphalt allowing it to flow and seal the damage essentially melting the cracks shut this method has already been tested in parts of the netherlands and germany with promising results another innovative strategy includes embedding microcapsules filled with healing agents like rejuvenating bitumen or polymerbased materials into road surfaces when cracks appear these capsules rupture and release their contents which seep into the fissures and restore the materials structural integrity a particularly fascinating development involves the use of bacteriabased concrete researchers have discovered that certain strains of bacteria when added to concrete mixtures in a dormant state can be activated by water that seeps into cracks upon activation these bacteria produce limestone effectively filling the cracks and preventing further damage this method mimics biological healing and holds great promise for bridges tunnels and other concreteheavy infrastructure other systems are also being developed where plantbased oils or synthetic rejuvenators are released from fibers or capsules within the asphalt to refresh the binder material as it ages maintaining elasticity and reducing brittleness countries like germany are already running smallscale trials to evaluate the longterm performance of these materials under real traffic conditions the netherlands has taken the lead in applying inductionbased healing asphalt on actual roadways and is aiming to scale this technology nationwide in the coming decades the united kingdom china south korea and the united states are also investing in various forms of selfhealing infrastructure from bioconcrete to smart asphalt capable of sensing and reporting damage autonomously the benefits of selfhealing roads extend far beyond simple durability they can reduce the frequency and cost of road repairs lower carbon emissions from construction activities and enhance overall road safety by minimizing the time roads are under maintenance with fewer roadworks and longerlasting surfaces both commuters and governments stand to benefit furthermore these technologies align with the goals of smart and sustainable urban planning where infrastructure is expected to be more resilient adaptive and environmentally conscious however challenges remain the upfront cost of selfhealing materials is still significantly higher than traditional materials and largescale implementation demands not only financial investment but also changes in construction standards and public policy questions about performance in extreme climates longterm behavior and recyclability of these new materials are still being researched yet despite these obstacles the momentum behind selfhealing infrastructure is undeniable in the near future roads that heal themselves could become an integral part of our citiesless prone to damage more environmentally friendly and capable of serving society for decades with minimal upkeep as technological advancements continue to push boundaries selfhealing roads may well represent the beginning of a smarter more sustainable era in global infrastructure

park service erases climate facts at fort sumter where the civil war began fort sumter an imposing island fortress in south carolina was bombarded by confederate forces at the start of the civil war now it faces a more modern threat rising seas fueled by climate change could leave much of the site underwater by the end of the century but the average visitor to fort sumter might not learn about this existential threat thats because the national park service has removed a sign that detailed the risks the site faces from climate change to comply with a directive from president trump according to three federal employees briefed on the matter the park service which manages the site took down the sign this month from the pier where visitors arrive by ferry at fort sumter which is on an artificial island in charleston harbor said the three federal employees who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they feared retaliation in an executive order in march mr trump directed the park service to review plaques films and other materials presented to visitors at 433 sites around the country it said that these materials should not inappropriately disparage americans and that they should emphasize the progress of the american people as well as the beauty abundance and grandeur of the american landscape elizabeth peace a spokeswoman for the interior department the parent agency of the park service did not comment on the removal of the sign at fort sumter but she said that in general the park service is taking action to remove or revise interpretive materials to ensure accuracy honesty and alignment with shared national values the sign at fort sumter said that as the earths climate changes rising seas could inundate most of the forts walls and flood the parade ground the open area on the forts lower level where soldiers used to assemble the parade ground would be constantly submerged the sign said if the mean sea level of charleston harbor were to rise by 4 feet researchers have estimated that the mean sea level of the harbor could rise by at least 33 feet or one meter by 2100 fort sumter is part of the fort sumter and fort moultrie national historical park in 2016 the park service worked with researchers at western carolina university to study the parks exposure to the effects of climate change including sea level rise coastal erosion flooding and storm surge the findings were grim the researchers classified more than a dozen structures in the park as highly vulnerable to the ravages of global warming they found that it would cost more than 11 billion to replace all of these structures including buildings docks roads and parking lots the us army corps of engineers has already joined with the park service to repair the sea walls surrounding fort sumter which were built in the 1800s saltwater erosion and surging tides have gnawed at the sea walls over the past several decades causing some rocks to crumble robert s young who directs the program for the study of developed shorelines at western carolina university said he wished the park service had not removed the sign because it informed visitors of a pressing threat to the entire region we need to prepare for a meter or more of sea level rise and thats going to be lifechanging for people who want to live and conduct business on the charleston peninsula dr young said kristen brengel the senior vice president for government affairs at the national parks conservation association an advocacy group accused the trump administration of censoring climate science at the park there was no justifiable reason to remove a sign that educates visitors about the changes they are seeing to fort sumter with their very eyes ms brengel said in an email for years national park service staff have been raising the alarm about the threat sea level rise poses to fort sumter they have worked tirelessly to protect this priceless place the trump administration has directed other
